newsitem.title: GHANA: Close race in Ghana poll.
newsitem.headline: Close race in Ghana poll.

text.p: Ghana's populist president Jerry Rawlings looked to have a fight on his hands on Sunday with his main opposition rival John Kufuor and his party edging into an early lead after presidential and parliamentary elections.

Provisional results from Saturday's elections showed that with just 6.5 percent of constituencies declared, Kufuor's New Patriotic Party had won eight of parliament's 200 seats and Rawlings's National Democratic Congress just five.
Employment and Social Welfare Minister David Sarpong Boateng lost his seat as did the government chief whip.
In the presidential race, Kufuor, a seasoned politician and a businessman, took the medium-sized provincial towns of Cape Coast, Sekondi, Sunyani, Koforidua and part of Tamale.

Unofficial returns from a handful of polling stations in the capital Accra showed Rawlings, who is bidding for a final four-year term, taking a lead in more populous poorer areas with Kufuor edging ahead in wealthier districts.
One result from Kufuor's stronghold in Kumasi, Ghana's second city and capital of the mighty pre-colonial Ashanti empire, suggested that he could look forward to a landslide there.
Ghanaians voted peacefully and in large numbers on Saturday. National Election Commission chairman Kwadwo Afari-Gyan told Reuters on Sunday that the estimated turnout was 70 percent.
Pundits gave little chance to the third contender, surgeon Edward Mahama of the People's National Convention, but his presence could force a run-off.

Rawlings, who has been called everything from a dictator to a messiah, twice seized power in the former British colony and once executed three former heads of state. He made the transition to elected president in disputed 1992 elections.
